text:
The salt does not forget the shape of stone,
Nor how the marble columns held their breath.
Below the waves, a kingdom sits alone,
Preserving life within its watery death.

The kelp grows thick across the market square,
Where merchants bargained once for gold and grain;
Now only shadows dance in brine-wrapped air,
And silence answers every silent pain.

The moon pulls tides that wash the empty gates,
A rhythmic pulse against the coral skin;
She counts the years the ocean imitates
The heartbeat of the world she’s trapped within.

No voice remains to beg for mercy’s ear,
Yet memory is sharper than fear.
